RoomType.rationale: InkletsNormal.RoomType => RoomType.Monster (InkletsNormal.cs:9). Sim carries no room_type field on the Encounter dataclass; 'inklets_normal' is placed in rooms.py:148-153's normal_keys for _overgrowth_rooms() (seam/rooms_and_map owns the picker itself). GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]=(10,20) (rewards.py:171) matches EncounterModel.cs:70/89's Monster=>10/20 defaults, which InkletsNormal does not override.

AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: No sim counterpart. C#'s only consumers of AllPossibleMonsters are ActModel.AllMonsters (ActModel.cs:169, read only by ModelDb.Monsters -> UnlockConsoleCmd.cs:68/147's dev-console 'monsters' listing and NGeneralStatsGrid.cs:164's stats-screen ratio label) and the Bestiary screen (NBestiary.cs:194) -- all UI/dev-console, zero gameplay or RNG effect, confirmed by reading every caller in src/. The headless sim has neither surface, so omitting a counterpart costs nothing observable.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: InkletsNormal.GenerateMonsters (InkletsNormal.cs:13-25) constructs `item` (plain Inklet), `inklet` (plain Inklet, then `.MiddleInklet = true`), `item2` (plain Inklet) IN THAT CONSTRUCTION ORDER, then returns [(item,null),(inklet,null),(item2,null)] -- add-order [normal, middle, normal], zero base.Rng calls anywhere. INKLETS_NORMAL.monster_classes = [Inklet, partial(Inklet, is_middle=True), Inklet] (inklets.py:72-75) is the SAME order [normal, middle, normal] with zero RNG draws in create_monsters (the default implementation this encounter inherits, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py). This is exactly the shape the brief flags as a known past bug class (Inklet add-order); re-checked here against current code and found correct -- the three-element order, the single 'middle' flag on the SECOND constructed instance, the null slots, and the zero draw count all match element-by-element.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: (structural -- Encounter dataclass has no hook methods)
ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden by InkletsNormal. The sim's Encounter dataclass (sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) declares no hook methods and is never passed to HookSystem.register -- it is plain data, structurally incapable of joining the hook walk, which reproduces 'the encounter itself is not a listener' exactly.

guards.what: MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward gold ladder (the encounter brief's 5th thing to verdict)
guards.rationale: InkletsNormal does not override MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward, so both inherit EncounterModel.cs:64-100's RoomType ladder (Monster=10-20) times AscensionHelper.PovertyAscensionGoldMultiplier under AscensionLevel.Poverty. INKLETS_NORMAL carries min_gold=None, max_gold=None (Encounter dataclass default, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py), so rewards.py:886-887 falls back to GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]=(10,20) (rewards.py:171) -- the same ladder. Ascension (Poverty) scaling is out of scope by the audit contract (rewards.py:32's explicit 'no Scarcity/Poverty scaling').

guards.what: EncounterModel.Rng independence (per the encounter brief: verify the sim does not draw encounter rolls off a shared/run-level stream)
guards.rationale: InkletsNormal.GenerateMonsters makes zero base.Rng calls (InkletsNormal.cs:13-25, confirmed by reading the whole method) and the sim's create_monsters counterpart (the default Encounter.create_monsters this unit inherits, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) makes zero calls to any Rng/random.Random for composition -- there is nothing here for stream identity to diverge on. (Draw-count fact only; which named stream backs EncounterModel.Rng in general is seam/rng_streams' mechanism, already verdicted faithful for the seeding formula at rng_streams step 21.)
